instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a 'lobbyist' as an individual who receives $2,000 or more in economic consideration in a calendar month (excluding reasonable travel reimbursements), establishing the compensation threshold for lobbyist status/registration.

Persons who make payments to influence legislative or administrative action must file if the payments total $5,000 or more in a calendar quarter, implying those below $5,000 (and not otherwise a lobbyist employer) are not required to file under this trigger.

The statute references a 10% of compensated time threshold for employees' time being included in reported payments, providing the only explicit percent-of-compensated-time threshold in the bundle relevant to time-based de minimis treatment.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled provisions defining 'lobbyist' (§82039) include a compensation threshold and a 'principal duties' standard, but do not set any lobbyist-definition expenditure threshold for registration.

The bundled text provides only a qualitative 'principal duties' standard in the lobbyist definition (§82039(a)(1)) and no quantifiable time threshold (hours/days/percent) that can be encoded as a TimeThresholdCell with magnitude and unit.
The reporting sections included (§§86112-86116) specify required information but do not state any per-item dollar de minimis threshold for itemizing lobbyist/lobbying-firm activity expenses.
